learning: If line_loss_events falls with the 16 mm footprint but progress stays low, the next limit is probably speed or steering at bends, so check steering_oscillation and max_error per track. If line loss does not fall, the footprint is not the cause, and the next test should be the span or the controller's line-loss handling.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's 16 mm footprint geometry. The controller is held at the iteration 1 values so that any change in score can be attributed to sensor_size. Sensor weights are matched to the sensor x order.
rationale: Iteration 1 (span ±0.03 m, 12 mm footprints, controller base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, kd 0.3) scored 69.32, up from 54.37. Line loss still occurs about once per run (1.65 on oval, 1.0 on s-bend and slalom), and max_error still reaches the 0.06 m limit. The Builder's iteration 2 geometry changes one variable, sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, with the ±0.03 m span, 15 mm spacing and 0.05 m forward offset unchanged. To keep that effect readable, I keep the iteration 1 controller exactly: base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.3, last_direction line loss, and weights -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1 matched to the x order of the sensors. The 16 mm footprint should keep the tape under an edge sensor for longer as the line crosses the array, which is the mechanism the Builder proposed for reducing abrupt loss. Expected result is fewer line-loss events and higher progress, but this is a prediction and has not been measured. I request the full measurement set, including controller_errors and noise_robustness, so the next race can separate line-loss behaviour from speed and oscillation.
